item.title: Several soldiers feared dead in Yobe road crash
item.description: By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman Several soldiers are feared dead, while others sustained injuries in a road accident involving a military vehicle at Garin Malam Adamu, near Buni Yadi, headquarters of Gujba Local Government Area of Yobe State. The accident reportedly occurred on Friday, November 20, while the soldiers were travelling from Buni Yadi to Damaturu, the state capital. The victims were reportedly evacuated to the Yobe State University Teaching Hospital, Damaturu, for medical attention. Although the exact casualty figure remains unknown, preliminary accounts have linked the accident to the poor condition of the affected section of the road. As of the time of filing this report, military authorities had yet to officially confirm the incident or disclose the number of casualties. The post Several soldiers feared dead in Yobe road crash appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Customs seize contraband worth N3.52bn in Ogun
item.description: .recover cannabis, codeine syrup, others By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Ogun I Area Command, has intercepted and seized contraband goods with a total Duty Paid Value (DPV) of ₦3.52 billion as part of intensified efforts to curb smuggling, protect public health and safeguard the nation’s economy. The seizures, which include 6,037 wraps of cannabis, 20,500 bottles of codeine-containing cough syrup, more than 1.45 million tablets and capsules of various brands, foreign parboiled rice, petroleum products and vehicles, were inspected and paraded by the Comptroller-General of Customs during a visit to the Command. According to a statement issued on Saturday, by the Public Relations Officer of Ogun I Area Command, Assistant Superintendent of Customs Paul Gimba, the total value of the seized items with available valuations stood at **₦3,517,838,700. The statement said the seizures reflected the Command’s sustained efforts to combat smuggling and prevent the circulation of prohibited and potentially harmful products in the country. A breakdown of the intercepted items showed that cannabis accounted for 6,037 wraps, valued at ₦1.268 billion, while 20,500 bottles of cough syrup containing codeine had a Duty Paid Value of ₦147.6 million. The Command also intercepted 828,920 tablets of different brands valued at ₦795.76 million and 627,320 capsules worth ₦376.39 million. Other pharmaceutical products seized included 2,850 ampoules of Enox 4000 injection, valued at ₦17.1 million, and 95 prostate pills worth ₦570,000. The seizures further included 5,173 bags of 50kg foreign parboiled rice, valued at ₦455.22 million, alongside 1,067 used tyres worth ₦52.82 million. In the petroleum products category, Customs intercepted 1,037 kegs of 25 litres of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), valued at ₦34.22 million, and 1,008 kegs of 25 litres of Automotive Gas Oil (AGO), worth ₦44.35 million. Other seized items comprised 21 packages of walkie-talkies, 185 packages of sanitary pads and diapers valued at ₦18.13 million, 125 live cartridges and two trucks with a combined valuation of ₦144 million. The Command also recorded seizures of several used vehicles, including a 2024 Toyota RAV4 and Toyota Highlander valued at a combined ₦50 million; two Lexus vehicles worth ₦25 million; a 2000 Toyota Hilux valued at ₦11 million; a 2013 Toyota RAV4 worth ₦17 million; and a Toyota Sienna valued at ₦14.7 million. Other vehicles intercepted were a 2010 Toyota Venza valued at ₦14.6 million, an Opel worth ₦7.3 million, a Mazda valued at ₦7.1 million and a 2012 Range Rover Sport worth ₦17.2 million. The Customs Service said the interceptions underscored the Command’s determination to enforce relevant Customs laws, prevent the importation and circulation of prohibited goods and protect Nigeria’s economic interests. item.title: Rising profile of Tems, Asake and Nigerian artists’ Grammy journey
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi The voices are getting louder everyday that Asake and Tems are the new King and Queen of Afrobeats respectively. And the Recording Academy confirmed it on November 16, 2026 when it announced the nominees for 2027 Grammy awards. Asake appears just to be coming to his own with two nominations while Tems shatfers the roof with four Grammy nominations in one year. Tems has emerged as Nigeria’s most successful representative in the latest nomination cycle, earning four nominations and further establishing herself as one of the most versatile Nigerian musicians on the international stage. Her recognition in the R&B categories is particularly noteworthy. It demonstrates that her appeal extends beyond the African music market and that her songwriting and vocal abilities are attracting recognition in mainstream American music. The nominations also build on an impressive Grammy history. Tems won her first Grammy in 2023 for her contribution to Future’s “Wait For U”, featuring Drake, which won Best Melodic Rap Performance. She subsequently won Best African Music Performance in 2025 for her reimagining of “Love Me JeJe”. She has also received recognition for her contribution to Beyoncé’s Renaissance, Wizkid’s “Essence” and Rihanna’s “Lift Me Up”, from the Black Panther: Wakanda Forever soundtrack. With two Grammy victories already to her credit, Tems is approaching the 2027 ceremony with an opportunity to increase her collection and further strengthen Nigeria’s presence in international R&B. Asake on the other hand has not won any Grammy – yet. But he appears to be knocking on the door. The “Lonely at the Top” hitmaker has now received four Grammy Award nominations as of November 2026. His nominations are all in the Best African Music Performance category. His flirting with the Recording Academy started in 2024 with his hit “Amapiano” with Olamide, followed by “MMS” with Wizkid in 2025. Once again, he has dragged Wizkid onto the Grammy ballot with their collaboration “Jogodo” and his own solo hit “Gratitude” in 2027 Six Nigerian stars earn 2027 Grammy nominations as Afrobeats expands global reach, with the country securing representation in Best African Music Performance, Best Global Music Album, Best Global Music Performance and Best R&B Song. Joining Tems and Asake on the list are: Burna Boy with one nomination for Dia Dia with Shakira for Best Global Music Performance; Wizkid has one nomination too, for his collaboration with Asake on “Jogodo”; Ayra Starr has two nominations for Best Global Music Album with her hit “Starrgirl” and Best African Music Performance on the “Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?)” collaboration with Angélique Kidjo and Davido with one nomination as his album “Oriadé” earned a place in the Best Global Music Album category, where it will compete against projects by Tems, Ayra Starr, Anitta and Angélique Kidjo. item.description: …tasks police on arrest, prosecution of culprits By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun has condemned the attack on Nigeria’s football legend and Ogun State Sports Ambassador, Chief Segun Odegbami, calling on the police to ensure that those responsible are apprehended and brought to justice. The Governor expressed deep concern over the incident, describing the attack on the former Super Eagles captain as unfortunate, unacceptable and a threat to the safety of citizens. Abiodun, however, thanked God that the assailants were unable to silence Chief Odegbami, noting that it was a matter of relief that the celebrated sports icon survived the attack. He said Odegbami, fondly known as ‘Mathematical’, remains an outstanding Nigerian whose contributions to the development of sports, particularly football, have earned him national and international recognition. The governor noted that as Ogun State’s Sports Ambassador, Odegbami occupies a special place in the state’s sports development agenda, adding that his experience, influence and enduring commitment to the promotion of sports remain invaluable. Abiodun urged the security agencies, particularly the police, to conduct a thorough investigation into the incident, track down the perpetrators and ensure that they face the full weight of the law. He stressed that no individual or group should take the law into their hands, warning that acts of violence and criminal intimidation would not be tolerated in Ogun State. The governor also wished Chief Odegbami continued strength and good health, assuring him of the state government’s concern and support. He reiterated his administration’s commitment to protecting lives and property and ensuring that Ogun State remains a peaceful and secure environment for residents and visitors. Meanwhile, the State Commissioner of Police, Bode Ojajuni, has assured the football legend that the perpetrators of his attack would be identified and brought to justice. Ojajuni, who gave the assurance, when Odegbami, following an attack on him, at his residence in Abeokuta, noted that visit was aimed at expressing the sympathy of the Ogun State Police Command over the incident and reassuring the former Nigerian international of the police commitment to protecting lives and property across the state. During the visit, Ojajuni reportedly conveyed his concern over the incident and wished Odegbami continued recovery and while assuring him that the command was treating the matter with the seriousness it deserved. The police commissioner disclosed that he had directed an immediate and comprehensive investigation into the incident to establish the circumstances surrounding the attack and identify those responsible. He also assured the former football star that the Command would deploy all necessary investigative resources to ensure that the perpetrators were apprehended and made to face the full weight of the law. item.title: ‘I Struggled To Come Out, Lost My Sister, Other Relatives,’ Bayelsa Boat Accident Survivor
item.description: A survivor of Friday’s boat accident in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has recounted how she struggled to escape from the capsized vessel, saying she lost several members of her family and neighbours in the tragedy. The woman, whose identity was not immediately disclosed, said her elder sister, her sister’s daughter-in-law and two children belonging to her relatives and neighbours were among those who died in the accident. Recounting the incident, she said the boat suddenly capsized, trapping passengers beneath it. “The boat just fell and pressed all of us. My elder sister’s son’s wife was lost. My elder sister was lost. Her son was also lost. One of my neighbours who followed us also lost her son. My neighbour herself was lost,” she said. ﻿ The survivor said she was the only person among those close to her who made it out alive, adding that she struggled to escape after the boat overturned. “It’s only me that is safe. When I came out, somebody held me. I was drinking water. I was not able to come out. I struggled before I came out. Where we were standing, the boat broke from above and pressed us down,” she said. Asked by the Bayelsa governor, Douye Diri, whether the bodies of her missing relatives and neighbours had been recovered, she replied in the negative. Her account comes as the death toll from the accident has risen to 23, while 24 survivors are receiving treatment in hospitals. The accident occurred near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw when a boat conveying mourners from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony capsized at about 11 a.m. on Friday. ﻿ The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident, saying preliminary findings indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways. However, a survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger vessel, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings, raising concerns about possible breaches of waterway safety regulations. President Bola Tinubu has expressed condolences to the families of the victims and directed relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery operations. In a statement posted on his X account, Tinubu described the incident as tragic and said those who died did not deserve to lose their lives in such circumstances. “Those who lost their lives in the tragedy did not deserve to die that way. I have directed all relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful recovery and rescue operation,” he said. The President also directed that Saturday’s presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, be held without much fanfare in honour of the victims. Meanwhile, Governor Diri has visited the scene of the accident and is expected to initiate an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. item.title: Can Enzo Maresca Win The Premier League In His First Season At Man City?
item.description: Six league titles. Ten years. A stand at the Etihad with his name on it. Good luck following that. Enzo Maresca has to, after Manchester City unveiled him as manager back in June 2026. Maresca at least knows his way around the training ground. Back in 2020-2021, he ran the Elite Development Squad and won Premier League 2 with them. He returned in 2022 to work under Guardiola as an assistant, and that season ended with the treble. So this is spell number three, and he’s tied down until 2029. Expectations at City don’t reset just because the man in the dugout has changed. City’s title odds have become some of the most debated in premier league online betting markets because bookmakers must weigh a campaign shaped as much by events off the pitch as on it. A Flying Start, Then A Bump The opening weeks went better than almost anyone expected. Maresca became the first manager in Premier League history to win his first seven games in charge of a new club. The football looked familiar too. City kept the ball and wore teams down, which is no surprise from a coach who learned so much from Guardiola. His Leicester and Chelsea sides played the same way. City spent big to help him. Their summer outlay of around £460 million was a record for any club, and £125 million of it went on Enzo Fernández from Chelsea, a fee that matched the Premier League transfer record. Phil Foden signed a four-year extension. Rodri, one of the faces of the Guardiola years, left for Barcelona. Maresca has won quickly before. He lifted the Championship title with Leicester in 2023-24. A year later at Chelsea, he won the Conference League and the Club World Cup and still finished fourth in the league. Seven straight wins at the start of a season guarantee nothing, of course. Plenty of fast starters have slid down the Premier League table once the winter fixtures arrive. City soon lost three league games in a row, one of them a 1-0 home defeat to Brighton, who had never won away at City before. Then there are Arsenal. Mikel Arteta, another former Guardiola assistant, ended their 22-year wait for the title in 2025-26, helped along by a Premier League record for goals from corners. Manchester City’s Italian manager Enzo Maresca gestures on the touchline during the English Premier League football match between Manchester City and Sunderland at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, north west England, on September 20, 2026. (Photo by PETER POWELL / AFP) The Fight Off the Pitch The bigger problem might be off the pitch entirely. Early in the 2026-27 season, an independent commission found City guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules. It ruled that the club used “sham” contracts with commercial partners to inflate revenues and cut costs by more than £900 million between 2009 and 2018. City deny any wrongdoing and have appealed. item.title: Bayelsa tragedy boat had no manifest, passengers didn’t wear life jacket – Diri
item.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa A visibly sad Governor of Bayelsa State, Senator Douye Diri, has revealed that the boat involved in the Friday fatal accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area had no manifest, and the passengers did wear life jackets. Consequently, Governor Diri vowed that all negligent persons involved will face trial. The governor gave the directive on Saturday after visiting the scene of the accident at the Oweikorogha axis of the river. Also, he visited survivors at the Government House Specialist Hospital in Yenagoa. He directed the Commissioner of Police, the State Director of the Department of State Services (DSS), and the Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy to commence investigation into the cause of the tragedy and submit a report in no distant time. Accompanied by Deputy Governor Dr. Peter Akpe, Deputy Speaker of the House of Assembly Michael Ogbere, and other top government officials, Diri in a statement by his Chief Press Secretary, Daniel Alabrah, condoled with bereaved families and affected communities. “On behalf of the state government, I extend our condolences to the families that have lost their loved ones and the communities that were affected. “I hear there were more victims from Ukubie community where the boat was headed, but several other communities were also affected. So our heartfelt and sincere condolences go to the communities, to the families, and the rest of the state,” he said. The governor described the incident as unfortunate and avoidable if every tier of government had done its job. “I believe that this should not have occurred if every department of government at the federal, state and local government diligently did their job. That is why I am going to institute a probe to ascertain what happened,” he said. Directing the Commissioner for Marine and Blue Economy, the Commissioner of Police and the DSS State Director to investigate, he said: “The Honourable Commissioner, within your ministry, there must be an investigation into this incident. “The Commissioner of Police and the State Director of DSS, I want a report; an investigative report on what happened. All those who have played one role or the other, the law must surely catch up with all of them.” Diri expressed shock that the boat had no manifest and did not board passengers from the designated point at the jetty in Ayama community. No safety measures He also lamented that none of the passengers wore safety vests, despite the availability of life jackets provided by the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy and the state government. “I cannot imagine a boat like that had no manifest and did not board passengers at the designated point. Today, we have this tragedy on our hands. “So, CP and DSS, you have work to do. I want that report in no distant date from now, so that people will know that there is a government in place here,” he said. item.title: Pain of losing loved ones never goes away – RMD
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Veteran actor Richard Mofe-Damijo, popularly known as RMD, has opened up about the emotional challenges of losing loved ones, describing grief as one of the hardest experiences he has had to deal with. The 65-year-old actor made this known during an appearance on At His Right Hand, a podcast hosted by Olive Emodi. Looking back at his personal experiences, RMD disclosed that losing his wife and mother remains a deeply painful part of his life. “Loss of dear people in my life is the hardest thing I have had to deal with. I have lost a wife, I have lost a mother. Loss is very difficult to deal with. The pain never goes away. “What happens is that the pain transitions, morphs into different things,” he said. Beyond grief, the actor also reflected on legacy and the responsibility of giving back, describing his current phase of life as one dedicated to pouring into others. “I am 65, and I am saying it’s your turn. One can always play an advisory role in nation building because you never stop building. I am in the legacy stage of my life. Just as people poured into my life, I think I need to pour into a lot of people’s lives,” he said. Speaking further about talent, the fashionable role interpreter maintained that natural abilities cannot remain suppressed indefinitely, insisting that talent will eventually find an outlet. “It’s a question of time. The stammerer will pronounce his or her father’s name. Same thing with talent. You can’t keep it down even if you try. Somehow, it will find its voice,” he said. item.title: Alcaraz to face Zverev for ATP Finals title
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz rallied past Ben Shelton on Saturday to book his spot in the ATP Finals title match, where he will meet world number one Alexander Zverev as he bids to lift the trophy for the first time. The world number three showed signs of vulnerability but fought through to beat the American 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 (7/1). He will play Zverev in Sunday’s decider, after the two-time Finals champion beat Daniil Medvedev 7-6 (7/0), 6-4 in the other last-four match-up. Alcaraz lost to Italian Jannik Sinner in the season-ender’s showpiece match last year and will aim to go one better this time around in Turin. He has been dealing with a left-thigh injury since Wednesday but, playing with his leg heavily strapped, he extended his winning streak to 13 matches, a run that includes title-winning campaigns in Vienna and Paris. However, it was a hard-fought victory as the Spaniard struggled to play with his usual freedom before pulling through in just over two hours. “I was a little bit frustrated at the beginning because I didn’t start the match the way that I wanted to, to be honest,” said the seven-time Grand Slam winner. “But I’m just happy that I came back in the second set… and ended up playing good tennis.” Having dropped only 15 games across his three round-robin matches without once losing his own serve, Alcaraz was broken in his very first service game against Shelton. The 23-year-old quickly fell behind 3-0 and was unable to claw his way back into the set. In the second frame, Alcaraz upped his level, gaining the upper hand by breaking to lead 5-3 before levelling at one set all. The deciding set remained tight, with neither player facing a break point, forcing the match into a tie-break. Shelton faltered with two unforced errors allowing the Spaniard to pull ahead 5-1, a deficit from which the American could not recover. “I think the third set was even closer. I think he raised the level a little bit from the second set, myself as well,” said Alcaraz. “Great points, great games, and just happy to play great tennis in the tie-breaker… I’m excited for tomorrow.” Earlier in the month, Alcaraz beat Shelton in the Paris Masters final to win the title for the first time — a measure of revenge on the American who had ended his US Open title defence in September. Alcaraz, who missed a chunk of the season with a wrist issue, will nonetheless be able to end his year on a high if he can next beat the man who took his French Open title during his injury-enforced absence. In claiming that title in Paris, as well as the US Open crown, Zverev catapulted himself above Alcaraz and Sinner in the rankings to world No. 1. In a repeat of the 2021 Finals title match, which the 29-year-old German also won, Zverev saw off Russian Medvedev in straight sets. A tightly-contested first frame rattled to a tie-break, which the two-time major winner raced through as Medvedev crumbled, failing to win a point. item.title: Tinubu doing fantastic job on sports infrastructure, says Infantino
item.description: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has commended President Bola Tinubu’s administration for its investment in sports infrastructure, describing its efforts as a “fantastic job” and an indication of Nigeria’s commitment to the future of its young population. Infantino gave the commendation on Saturday while addressing the 48th Ordinary General Assembly of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) in Abuja. The FIFA president urged members of the Nigerian delegation to convey his regards to Tinubu, while acknowledging the contributions of the President and other Nigerian leaders to sports development. “On behalf of President Tinubu, please send him our warmest regards. He is doing together with all of you. Fantastic job here in Nigeria, showing that you are a country projected into the future,” Infantino said. He particularly praised investments in sports facilities, noting that they reflected confidence in the potential of young Nigerians. “We were discussing this yesterday as well, also with the Chairman of the National Sports Commission, my brother Shehu. The investments done in sports facilities infrastructure show that you believe in your youth, in the young girls and the young boys of Nigeria,” he said. “Thank you for that. Congratulations for that,” he added. Infantino also thanked Nigeria for hosting him and his delegation, which included FIFA Secretary-General Mattias Grafström, describing the visit as an opportunity to reconnect with the continent. “Thanks for welcoming me and our delegation with the Secretary-General and the others here at home in Africa, in Abuja. Thank you for your support. It means the world to me,” he said. His remarks followed an inspection of sports infrastructure projects in Nigeria on Friday, including the remodelled Warri City Stadium and the Hussey College mini-stadium and sports complex in Delta State. He also visited the ongoing FIFA Forward Technical Centre project at the Moshood Abiola National Stadium in Abuja, describing the facility as an investment in the future of Nigerian football. “This is a collaboration between Nigerian football and FIFA for the future of the girls and the boys of Nigeria,” he said. During his visit to the Warri City Stadium, Infantino stressed the importance of developing grassroots sports facilities to ensure that football remained accessible to people across communities. “That’s what football is about. It’s for everyone, everywhere. It’s the big stadiums, it’s the World Cup, but it’s also the smaller stadiums, it’s the proximity,” he said. The FIFA president also expressed appreciation for the reception he received in Nigeria, assuring the country of the world football governing body’s continued support. “I feel so much the love of Africa, the love of Nigeria. I am very happy to be here. You can always count on FIFA. We are not just your partners; we are your family members,” he added. Infantino’s visit also coincided with Nigeria’s endorsement of his bid for another term as FIFA

item.title: Odukoya drags sister, others to court over removal as senior pastor
item.description: The Senior Pastor of the Fountain of Life Church, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya, has dragged his sister and others before a Federal High Court in Lagos, challenging his purported removal from office and the decisions taken by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees. Odukoya, alongside the Incorporated Trustees of the Fountain of Life Church, instituted the action against eight defendants, including Pastor Tolu Odukoya, Mr Biodun Balogun, Mr Biodun Awosika, Pastor Rotimi Okpaise, Pastor Tobi Enuha, Pastor Gbenga Onabanjo, Pastor Fred Ohiani and Pastor Akin Osinbajo. This is coming some days after a Lagos State High Court had restrained him from parading as the senior pastor in the church. Odukoya in an affidavit in support of the applications is asking the court to determine whether meetings held by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees on January 22, February 28 and November 16, 2026, and the decisions taken at those meetings complied with the church’s constitution. Odukoya said he was appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees at an emergency meeting of the board on September 14, 2023, and was subsequently installed in September of the same year. He said the church and its organs were governed by its constitution, amended by a special resolution dated January 16, 2003, and that the defendants were members of its Board of Trustees. According to his affidavit, the disagreement began after a December 19, 2025, meeting of the board, attended by Bishop Mike Okonkwo, at which the possibility of handing over the church’s administrative arm to the Associate Senior Pastor was discussed. He said no resolution or final decision was reached at the meeting. Board meeting Odukoya said he subsequently convened a board meeting for January 5, 2026, but it could not hold because there was no quorum. He added that some trustees later presented proposals to him, many of which he declined because, according to him, they were inconsistent with the church’s constitution. He said the trustees subsequently sent him a letter dated January 7, 2026, requesting a response within three days, but he did not see it until after the deadline had elapsed. Odukoya said he later directed the board secretary to schedule a meeting for January 30, 2026, after a request for a special meeting was made by a board member. However, he alleged that a separate notice for a meeting on January 22 was circulated by the fourth defendant and did not come from the board secretariat. “I received the notice late in the evening of January 20, 2026, effectively giving me one day notice of the purported meeting,” he stated. He said he declined to attend the meeting, but the defendants proceeded with it under the name of “concerned members of the Board”. item.title: Arsenal held by Newcastle rally and lose Raya to injury
item.description: Arsenal missed the chance to open up an eight-point lead at the top of the Premier League after a stirring second-half fightback from Newcastle held the defending champions to a 2-2 draw on Saturday. The Gunners led through Eberechi Eze’s strike after a dominant first 45 minutes. But Mikel Arteta’s men were suddenly headed for defeat when goals from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw provided a much-needed boost for under-fire Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle. Noni Madueke salvaged a point for Arsenal and stretched their lead at the top over surprise package Brighton to six points. However, the loss of influential goalkeeper David Raya to injury could provide a twist in the title race that many believed Arsenal would cruise. Newcastle remain in the bottom half of the table with just one win in six games in all competitions. Yet, Jaissle can point to his side’s second half performance as a potential turning point after a difficult start to his reign at St. James’ Park. Arsenal move back six points clear of third-placed Manchester City, but missed the chance to put their foot down in the defence of their title. Madueke continued his impressive form in the injury absence of Bukayo Saka and hit the post early on. Former Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes was roundly booed on his first return to Tyneside since making a £75 million ($98 million) move to the Emirates Stadium In August. The Brazilian nearly silenced his former faithful when he prodded just wide from a Madueke cross as Arsenal pressed for the opener. It duly arrived 10 minutes before the break when Kai Havertz pounced on a poor touch by Lewis Hall and brilliantly played in Eze to blast high past Lukas Hornicek. Jaissle got the response he needed from his half-time team talk as Newcastle came out a completely different proposition after the break. Arsenal also played a part in letting the home side back into the game and lifting the 50,000 crowd in doing so. Martin Odegaard shanked his attempt at a long ball forward to allow William Osula to play in Barnes to level. Suddenly an Arsenal side that had kept seven clean sheets in their opening 10 league games was on the rocks. Thiaw bundled home a second for Newcastle just 13 minutes later after Dan Burn was left completely unmarked from a corner and his header was only parried by Raya. That proved to be one of Raya’s final interventions as the Spaniard had to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga. Raya would be a massive miss if the Spaniard is sidelined for a significant spell. But Arsenal regained their composure in time to salvage a point that keeps them well in the driving seat to retain the title. Odegaard made amends for his earlier error by freeing Madueke down the right and he cut inside before his tame deflected shot found a way past Hornicek. item.title: Death Toll In Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 23
item.description: The death toll from Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 23, with 24 survivors receiving treatment in hospitals. The accident occurred when a boat conveying mourners to a burial ceremony capsized near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw. The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident in a statement, saying the boat was travelling from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony on Friday, when it capsized at about 11 a.m. A preliminary police report indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways. Following the incident, rescue operations were launched, with several passengers rescued while others were initially reported missing. A survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger boat, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings, suggesting that this might have contributed to the accident. President Bola Tinubu has expressed condolences to the families of the victims, describing the incident as tragic and directing relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery efforts. In a statement posted on his X account, Tinubu said, “Those who lost their lives in the tragedy did not deserve to die that way. I have directed all relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful recovery and rescue operation.” The President also directed that the presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, on Saturday, be held without much fanfare in honour of those who lost their lives. “On behalf of the entire nation, I mourn those who lost their lives in the incident and sympathise with their families, the government and the people of Bayelsa State. “I particularly mourn with Governor Douye Diri over this sad incident. I pray that God Almighty repose their souls and comfort their families,” he said. Meanwhile, Governor Douye Diri has visited the scene of the accident and is expected to initiate a probe into the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. The state government has also warned boat operators against overloading, reckless navigation and travelling without life jackets, stressing the need for strict compliance with waterway safety regulations. It also emphasised the importance of enforcing safety measures to prevent a recurrence of such incidents. ﻿ The post Death Toll In Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 23 appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: 2027 Election: INEC failed on voters’ register – ADC
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The African Democratic Congress, ADC, has described the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC’s decision to postpone the clean-up of the national voters’ register until after the 2027 general elections as a major failure. The party said INEC had four years to prepare for the exercise. However, ADC said the voters’ register is only one of several issues that will determine the credibility of the 2027 elections. They pointed to electronic transmission of results, result collation and compliance with the Electoral Act as other major areas of concern. Speaking to Vanguard, the ADC National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, said INEC’s failure to clean up the register raised questions about its commitment to conducting credible elections. “This shouldn’t have happened. INEC had four years to prepare and plan for this, and its failure to do so does not suggest that it is taking its responsibilities seriously, particularly the issue of maintaining a credible voters’ register,” he said. Abdullahi, however, said the party would not make the outcome of the 2027 elections depend solely on whether INEC produced a credible voters’ register, noting that previous elections had been conducted despite imperfections in the register. “We do not believe that the credibility of the 2027 general election rests solely on INEC’s ability to produce a credible voters’ register. It would have given everyone greater confidence if the commission had been able to do so, but we are not going to hinge the fate of the 2027 election on that single issue.” He said the ADC was also concerned about how INEC would implement the Electoral Act, particularly the electronic transmission of results from polling units, the collation process and the duties of electoral officers regarding Forms EC8A and EC8E. “There are other, more pertinent issues of concern to our party. These include compliance with the Electoral Act, the electronic transmission of results from polling units, the collation of results and the additional responsibilities assigned to electoral officers regarding Forms EC8A and EC8E.” On the possible effect of the voters’ register on the elections, Abdullahi argued that strict compliance with the law, particularly provisions on voter accreditation, could reduce the impact of its shortcomings. “If INEC complies with the Electoral Act, particularly regarding voter accreditation, the shortcomings in the voters’ register may not have as much impact. Problems arise when the commission fails to abide by its own rules and the provisions of the Electoral Act,” he said. He said the ADC was studying possible weaknesses in the electoral process and making arrangements to ensure that its votes were protected. “We know where the loopholes are, and that is why we continue to focus on them and ensure that we make adequate arrangements to protect our votes.” Vanguard News The post 2027 Election: INEC failed on voters’ register – ADC appeared first

item.title: China Diaries: The Railway Connecting Continents
item.description: Standing at the Xi’an International Port Station in northwest China, watching the movement of freight trains preparing to transport goods across borders and continents, I was reminded that economic development is not only about what a country produces. It is also about how efficiently it can move what it produces to the rest of the world. Xi’an occupies an interesting place in China’s history. It was once the starting point of the ancient Silk Road, which connected China to Central Asia, the Middle East and Europe through centuries of trade and cultural exchange. Today, the city is reclaiming that historic role through a modern railway network that connects Chinese manufacturing centres to markets across Europe and Asia. The China-Europe Railway Express is one of the most visible outcomes of China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). Through this network, freight trains transport automobiles, electronics, machinery, textiles, agricultural products and other goods across the Eurasian continent. What makes the initiative particularly interesting is how it has transformed the economic possibilities of a city located thousands of kilometres from the sea. Xi’an has become an important international logistics hub, demonstrating that geographical distance from a coastline does not have to limit a city’s participation in global trade. The railway network has continued to expand. By November 2025, China-Europe freight trains had completed nearly 120,000 journeys, connecting 232 cities in 26 European countries and more than 100 cities in 11 Asian countries. The value of goods transported through the network had reached $426.4 billion by the end of 2024. These are not merely impressive transportation figures. They represent an evolving system of economic connectivity, linking manufacturers, suppliers, distributors and consumers across national borders. Beyond transportation: The economics of connectivity The significance of the railway goes beyond moving containers from one destination to another. It creates opportunities for businesses to reach markets faster, diversify their supply chains and reduce their dependence on a single transportation route. Rail freight offers an important middle ground between air and sea transportation. While it is generally more expensive than shipping by sea, it can be considerably faster. For certain categories of goods, particularly machinery, automobile components, electronics and other time-sensitive products, that difference can be commercially significant. It also provides an alternative when disruptions affect other transportation routes. Another important feature is the development of inland logistics infrastructure. Warehousing, customs processing, container handling, industrial parks and distribution services have grown around railway connections. item.title: Chelsea Humbled As Leeds Run Riot
item.description: Chelsea suffered an embarrassing 4-1 defeat against Leeds on Saturday as the Blues were beaten for the third time in their last four Premier League matches. Xabi Alonso’s side were ripped apart by rampant Leeds, who savoured their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years. Chelsea scored six in a League Cup win against Leeds in September, but Daniel Farke’s men erased that painful result with a superb display on their return to West London. Just 24 hours after NFL legend Tom Brady was linked with buying a minority stake in Chelsea, the seven-time Super Bowl winner might be thinking twice about his mooted investment. Leeds United’s English goalkeeper #01 James Trafford and Leeds United’s Swiss striker #19 Noah Okafor celebrate after the English Premier League football match between Chelsea and Leeds United at Stamford Bridge in London on November 21, 2026. (Photo by Henry NICHOLLS / AFP) Brady is believed to be friendly with Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali, who will have a big decision to make on Alonso’s future if results do not improve soon. Chelsea are languishing in eighth place after a fifth defeat in their 11 league games under Alonso, who was hyped as the stabilising force the club needed after a turbulent period. Alonso has been hampered by the absence of injured Brazilian striker Joao Pedro in recent weeks, and once again Chelsea struggled without their attacking talisman. Making his full debut in Alonso’s latest bid to find a stand-in for Pedro, Emmanuel Emegha fired Chelsea ahead in the 25th minute. Yet within three minutes they gifted an equaliser to Noah Okafor, who punished static defending to lash home. Morgan Rogers conceded a penalty eight minutes into the second half, and Dominic Calvert-Lewin converted to put Leeds in front. Swiss striker Okafor quickly made it three in the 58th minute and Brenden Aaronson got a fourth in stoppage time to leave Chelsea in turmoil. Over a miserable five-match spell, the Blues have lost to Tottenham, Sunderland and Leeds, while also crashing out of the League Cup against Liverpool. While it is too soon to suggest Alonso is in danger of the sack, the Spaniard has endured a disappointing start to his first spell as a Premier League manager. Failing to beat struggling pair Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two games would undoubtedly turn the heat up on the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen boss.
